observations: Photo 0 shows the top-left of a silver and black camera with “Nikon” on the prism housing and “Z fc” on the top plate; the lens mount cap reads “Nikon Z mount”.
Photo 1 shows the shutter-speed dial, “Nikon” on the prism, “Z fc” on the top plate, and a lens mounted on the camera.
Photo 2 shows the camera body from above with the lens detached, plus a battery, battery charger, body cap, rear lens cap, and a front lens cap marked “TTArtisan APS-C 25mm F2.0”.
All three photos carry a watermark reading “OYIBEST GLOBAL RESOURCES” or “POSTED ON JIJI”.

claims.claim: Nikon Z fc retro-inspired SLR-style mirrorless camera.

claims.evidence: sensor specifications are not visible in any photo

risks.risk: Camera may not power on, focus, or take photos.
risks.proof: Video of the camera turning on, navigating menus, and firing the shutter.

risks.risk: Sensor may have dust, scratches, or dead pixels.
risks.proof: Photo of the sensor with the mirror locked up or a sensor-cleaning-mode video.

risks.risk: Lens may have fungus, separation, or scratches.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the lens front and rear elements in bright light.
risks.if_unproven: as lens faulty or not included

risks.risk: Battery and charger may not work.
risks.proof: Video of the battery charging and powering the camera.
risks.if_unproven: as no working battery or charger

proof_requests: Video of the camera powering on, showing the menu, and taking a photo.
Close-up photos of the lens glass front and rear.
Photo of the sensor or a shutter-count readout.
Video of the battery charging in the supplied charger.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Nikon Z fc mirrorless camera from the branding visible in the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case using comparable entry-level mirrorless cameras.
